title: Rabbi Yitzchak Atusha

paragraphs: He further merited to learn from Resh Lakish, as in Beitzah chapter 1, halakhah 9: he asked Resh Lakish, 'What is the law regarding grinding (לשחוק) kondiṭon on a festival day?' He said to him, 'Give me and I will drink.' This statement is not found in our Yerushalmi, but it is indeed cited thus in the Ran, Beitzah chapter 1, printed locator קפו:.[^1]

And his principal teacher was Rabbi Ze’ira (printed: ר״ז א׳), as in [Sotah, chapter 3, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sotah.3.1.5): 'Rabbi Ze’ira brought Rabbi Yitzchak Atusha, and he recited it for him.' And [Peah, chapter 8, halakhah 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.8.4.4): 'He said before Rabbi Ze’ira in the name of the school of Rabbi Yannai.'

And he had a son named Rabbi Chiyya, as in Terumot chapter 10, halakhah 6: 'Rabbi Yirmeyah instructed Rabbi Yitzchak Atusha,' and some say: 'Rabbi Chiyya son of Rabbi Yitzchak Atusha.' The author of Seder HaDorot wrote that he served as a reciter (tanna) for Rabbi Abba bar Memel, but was mistaken in this, as I explained in his entry.[^2]

notes.text: The parallel in [Yerushalmi Beitzah 1:9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Beitzah.1.9.3) concerns grinding konditon, but names Yitzchak Dihava and Rabbi Yochanan rather than Yitzchak Atusha and Resh Lakish.

[Terumot 10:6:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.10.6.11) names Rabbi Chiyya as the son of Rabbi Yitzchak Atushiyya in an account about blood in an egg; it differs from Hyman’s ruling and alternative recipient here.
